messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: static functions
parts:
Hi,

I have one function for the boxplot stuff that isn't for a particular
class and I don't really understand how to use setMethodS3 for it. I
could just make it a method for 'list' since the input needs to be that,
but it's not going to be a function with lots of methods for different
classes. So I think it needs to be a 'static' command, but I don't
understand how to set it up.

Currently I have the standard function definition,

convertBoxplotStats<-function(boxplotStats){
...
}

How would this convert over in setMethodS3?

(Maybe this is really a question for another list regarding the other
packages that aroma.affymetrix uses?)

Best,
Elizabeth

So, I guess you just suggested

setMethodS3("convertBoxplotStats", "list", function(boxplotStats, ...) {
...
})

yourself, which I think is slightly better than:

>
> Currently I have the standard function definition,
>
> convertBoxplotStats<-function(boxplotStats){
> ...
> }
>
> How would this convert over in setMethodS3?

I'm not sure about that turning it into a static method of a class
will make it better?!? What class would you then want to couple the
method to?

I'm not sure what the real problem is.

/Henrik

>
> (Maybe this is really a question for another list regarding the other
> packages that aroma.affymetrix uses?)
>
> Best,
> Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: static functions
parts:
Hi.

[I reply to the list because part of my reply is useful to others as well]

On Wed, Feb 20, 2008 at 2:06 PM, Elizabeth Purdom
<epu...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
> Okay, so I don't think I understand the concept of static function, but
> that's a different issue.

I borrow the concept of a "static method" from Java. It is a method
that "belongs" to a class and that you can call without having an
instance of that class. For instance, when we load a CEL set we do
not have an instance of AffymetrixCelSet available but we want to load
one, i.e.

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(...)

The alternative would be do do:

dummy <- AffymetrixCelSet()
cs <- byName(dummy, ...)

A more commonly seen solution in R for the above is to come up with a
long function name like:

cs <- setupAffymetrixCelSetByName(...)

but the it takes a human to infer that it actually returns an
AffymetrixCelSet, which is why we use static (class) method instead.

Another, more basic example, is when you use:

library(R.oo)
obj <- Object()
obj$foo <- 2
save(obj, file="foo.Rbin")

and later want to load that same Object:

library(R.oo)
obj <- Object$load("foo.Rbin")

>
> Regardless, I'm wondering is it bad to have .list method that doesn't
> assume that the list is a list of AffymetrixCelFile objects?
> plotDensity.list appears to assume this (my most recent post about
> this). But I think I need to take this offline, because this is perhaps
> just a developer's question. Repost it if you think best. And ignore
> this if I'm understanding the subsetting of the AffymetrixCelSet
> incorrectly -- or read my post first...

The problem is that the implementation in 'aroma.light' (just like
'limma', 'affy' etc) cannot know about 'aroma.affymetrix'. There are
plotDensity() implementation in 'aroma.light' for matrices and lists.
The 'list' implementation allows you to plot the density for numeric
vectors of different lengths. That the plotDensity() in
aroma.affymetrix has the same name is "just a coincidence".

Details: There is no way to setup an S3 method (neither a S4 method)
to "test" also for the class of each element of the list. That is
instead taken care of by the generic error detection in R, hence you
"strange" error message. It is still caught as an error though.

So, unfortunately, it is not easy to have a generic plotDensity()
function that operates on a list of either numeric vectors or other
data types/classes.

>
> Here's what I mean. I have made a function plotBoxplot with methods
> .QualityAssessment, .AffymetrixCelSet
> and .AffymetrixCelFile. I also have a function plotBoxplot.list which is
> used by these functions and roughly takes as the input a list of the
> output of boxplot.stats -- a list of things not related to any
> aroma.affymetrix object but just generally because of the akward nature
> of the required input to bxp. So it's a 'helper' function, but also
> something that allows the replotting of the output of these functions
> without doing the calculation. Example:
> out<-plotBoxplot(qam)
> calls the calculation function as well as plotBoxplot.list; out is a
> list of the output of the boxplot stats. Then
> plotBoxplot(out)
> will seamlessly replot it. So that's good, I think. And it's an awfully
> useful function in general, I must say, because I'm frequently wanting this.

So, ideally grDevices::boxplot.stats() would not just return a 'list'
but a list with class attribute c("BoxplotStats", "list"). Then you
could write the following to better control for the class:

setMethodS3("plotBoxplot", "BoxplotStats", function(obj, ...) {
< the current implementation you have >
})

>
> But shouldn't plotBoxplot.list take as input a list of AffymetrixCelFile
> and basically call plotBoxplot.AffymetrixCelFile on each of the entries,
> like plotDensity. Or is that just special to plotDensity? (you mentioned
> you wanted to get rid of any need for the arrays=... option)
> Logically, I should be able to call for an AffymetrixCelSet
> out<-plotBoxplot(cs[1:5])
> but this wouldn't work in how I have it now.
>
> My solution (unimplemented) is for plotBoxplot.list to check what kind
> of objects are in the list. Is this how I should do it?

See my explanation of plotDensity() for lists above and the trade-off
of choosing what it should do.

The easiest way to subset of arrays and still get what you want is:

out <- plotBoxplot(extract(cs, 1:5))

Details: extract(cs, 1:5) returns another AffymetrixCelSet with only
arrays 1 to 5. However, as we discussed offline, this will calculate
the summary only based on this subset.

The idea is to write a method for AffymetrixCelSet (or a subclass of
it) when you want to do something on a set of CEL files. Do not work
with a 'list' of CEL files (that is what the AffymetrixCelSet class is
for in the first place).

Please do not use '[' operators on AffymetrixCelSet objects etc,
because it is still not decided how they should work/be defined. [I
guess I should basically turn the off].

Ok, there are a lot of generic as well as specific details here, but I
hope I at least managed to guide in the right direction. If not, let
me know.

Henrik

> Elizabeth
